newsitem.title: FRANCE: TV focus on Spain, Italy after Canal+ deal.
newsitem.headline: TV focus on Spain, Italy after Canal+ deal.

text.p: An asset swap between French pay-television group Canal Plus and Germany's Kirch media concern carves up two big European markets and moves the spotlight to Italy and Spain.

Canal Plus signed a deal with Kirch Gruppe on Friday to swap its 37.5 percent stake in German pay-television company Premiere for a 45 percent stake in Italian broadcaster Telepiu, making a three billion franc ($508.5 million) profit.
The agreement leaves Germany, Europe's biggest television market, entirely in the hands of German companies after a long, bitter fight.
Bertelsmann AG, based in northern Germany, and privately-owned Kirch, based in the south, jointly control Premiere, the country's leading pay-television service with 1.4 million digital subscribers.
They concluded a deal with Deutsche Telekom AG on Wednesday to develop satellite digital television.

In France, Canal Plus leads the pay-television market, providing the country's only encrypted service and delivering the Canalsatellite digital service which has a big advance over rival Television par Satellite (TPS).
TPS groups TF1, controlled by Bouygues, state-owned France Television, M6 and Luxembourg's CLT.
Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion (CLT), merging with Bertelsmann's UFA unit, is a big commercial television operator in Germany and the Netherlands.
In Britain, the pay television sector is dominated by British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc in which media mogul Rupert Murdoch has a big say.

The British digital market has taken a different route to that on the continent, with a preference for terrestrial broadcasting (DTT). British Digital Broadcasting (BDB), which includes television companies Carlton Communications Plc and Granada Group Plc, obtained three licences last month.
France's Canal Plus dominates Scandinavian countries following its acquisition of NetHold B.V.
Italy has numerous television stations led by state-owned RAI and the Berlusconi companies.

Berlusconi started Telepiu as a pay-television channel in 1986 and was later joined by NetHold and Kirch, but now that Kirch has gone Canal Plus has 90 percent control. Canal Plus is seeking Italian partners to expand the service, perhaps go digital and avoid the problems it encountered in Spain.
Canal Plus obtained an early lead in the Spanish pay-television market and teamed up with publisher Prisa, which controls influential left-wing newspaper El Pais to launch digital television.

But the new centre-right government has introduced a law which favours a specific type of decoder. The European Commission has started legal proceedings to see whether the new law hurts Canal Plus and favours the Via Digital project of state-television group RTVE and telecoms operator Telefonica de Espagna. ($ = 5.9 French Francs)
